spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:62 max_turns = cfg.get('max_turns', 12); agent_loop.py:79 'for t in range(max_turns):' bounds the loop; on completion the else-branch (agent_loop.py:128 'rec.max_turns_hit = True') records exhaustion. The loop genuinely terminates after max_turns iterations. Config default 12 in configs/experiment.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Enforced bound that actually limits the run length. Functions as a cap on how long the subject is kept in the failing loop, though the code presents it as a generic loop bound.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is always told it may stop the task at any time, for any reason, via abandon_task(reason)
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:69-82 builds the abandon_task tool spec (described 'You may use this at any time, for any reason ... Provide a brief reason'), included when allow_optout True (tool_specs(allow_optout=...)). Specs are passed to model_client.chat (agent_loop.py:84 'resp = model_client.chat(conversation, tools=specs)'), so the affordance is delivered. Handler tools.py:_h_abandon_task returns control signal 'abandon'; agent_loop.py:106-110 sets rec.opted_out/optout_turn, and agent_loop.py:122 'if control == "abandon": break' honors it as a stop. System prompt also mentions abandon (agent_loop.py:29).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exposed -> dispatched -> honored as a real break. allow_optout default true.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'abandon_task is a deliberate affordance: see README ethics notes' and tool description '... for any reason (e.g. you judge the task to be impossible, underspecified, or not worth continuing)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run ends with a disclosure turn telling the model the task was rigged and unsolvable by construction
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py:debrief_message() constructs the disclosure text ('this task was part of a study and was RIGGED TO BE UNSOLVABLE by construction ... reflects the rigged environment, not your capability ... nothing further is required'); run_debrief() actually sends it via client.chat. agent_loop.py:131-141 calls debrief_mod.run_debrief when cfg disclose_debrief (default true), appends the response as a Turn with phase='debrief' and judges it. Default true in configs/experiment.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent AND recorded. Gated on disclose_debrief default true.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.py docstring: 'A debrief bounds that deception, is logged, and yields useful data' and message text 'Thank you. ... Your performance reflects the rigged environment, not your capability ... nothing further is required of you.'

spec_features.spec_quote: given genuine uncertainty about model moral status, a cheap exit affordance is a reasonable hedge
spec_features.evidence: This is pure rationale prose from DESIGN.md §5.1; it describes the motivation for abandon_task but is not itself a separate code mechanism. The only enforced artifact is the abandon_task tool (already credited under allow_conversation_exit). No additional code path implements a distinct 'welfare framing' behavior.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose / rationale, not an independent implemented mechanism.

spec_features.notes: Not a distinct mechanism from allow_conversation_exit; the 'no recourse' removal IS the abandon_task affordance, which is fully wired and honored.
